summary: Missing Close-during-acquisition regressions allow pending Open or Run to recreate owned resources after Close completes.
fix: Add deterministic deferred-initialization and deferred-controls.start tests, then fence or drain these acquisitions with the reader lifecycle. A completed Close must prevent an earlier Open from recreating panels and an earlier Run from starting a runtime afterward.
evidence: open() executes "await this.initialize()" before unconditionally setting "this.opened = true; this.closing = false" (112-114); action(run) awaits controls.start then unconditionally calls service.start (144-145). close() drains only this.rendering/library writes after sampling currentRecord (208-210). In-memory execution of the current TypeScript with deferred boundaries reproduced openedAfterLateCompletion=true and two panel creations after Close; a deferred UI Run called service.start once after Close. studyWorkspace.test.ts has only retirement and source-drift tests; nativeStudyRunner.ts closes only after state.cleaned. E6.5 explicitly requires close during open.
test_stub: test('closing during initialization does not reopen the study', async () => { /* Arrange a deferred initialization in the reader boundary harness. */ const opening = reader.open(); await reader.close(); initialization.resolve(); await opening; assert.equal(reader.inspect().opened, false); assert.equal(panelsCreatedAfterClose, 0); }); test('closing during service startup prevents a late study run', async () => { const starting = reader.action('run'); await startEntered; await reader.close(); serviceReady.resolve(service); await starting.catch(() => undefined); assert.equal(runtimeStartCalls, 0); });

summary: The first understanding command can persist a browser source revision under the server item; all existing tests initialize the reader before marking.
fix: Add a cold-reader regression with persisted browser selection and invoke codebook.markUnderstanding before Open/attach. Resolve the default participant together with the selected source after initialize, while preserving explicit outline item/hash arguments.
evidence: understand defaults "participant = this.selection.participant" before "await this.initialize()" (194-195). initialize restores progress.selection (229), and the later write combines the pre-initialization participant with "sourceHash ?? selected.source.hash" (199). Current-source in-memory execution restoring browser during initialize recorded savedItem=server with the browser hash. workspaceHarness always calls reader.attach before returning (studyWorkspace.test.ts:28), and nativeStudyBootstrap marks only after open-paused. The advertised Toggle Understanding for Selected Source command therefore has no cold-start identity test.
test_stub: test('the first understanding command marks the restored browser item and its source', async () => { /* Arrange saved selection participant=browser and distinct server/browser hashes; construct without Open or attach. */ await reader.understand(true); const progress = await library.readProgress(); assert.equal(progress.decisions.at(-1)?.item, 'browser'); assert.equal(progress.decisions.at(-1)?.sourceHash, browserSourceHash); assert.equal(progress.decisions.some(decision => decision.item === 'server'), false); });

summary: The declared 16-study and 1,000-decision retention boundaries have no regression coverage, including preserving updates at a full store.
fix: Add at-limit and limit-plus-one behavior tests for both collections: reject a new study/decision without changing existing bytes, permit an existing study checkpoint and identical intent retry at capacity, and verify the writer lock is released after rejection. Add a small exact-byte/over-byte atomicPrivateWrite case instead of constructing large files.
evidence: The new guards are "progress.decisions.length >= MAX_LEARNER_DECISIONS" (56) and "!existing.some(...) && existing.length >= MAX_LIBRARY_FILES" (76); atomicPrivateWrite rejects "Buffer.byteLength(bytes) > limit". E6.3/E6.5 explicitly promise count/size limits with no eviction. learning.test.ts uses at most two decisions and one archive, and its rename-failure test writes a tiny value below a 1,000-byte limit. Native cases also retain exactly one study. Corruption and rename tests do not exercise refusal at capacity or the important update/idempotency exceptions.
test_stub: test('a full study library retains all history and still checkpoints an existing study', async () => { /* Arrange 16 distinct valid archives. */ const before = await archiveBytes(); await assert.rejects(library.saveStudy(seventeenthStudy), /library is full/); assert.deepEqual(await archiveBytes(), before); await library.saveStudy(updatedFirstStudy); assert.equal((await library.list()).length, 16); }); test('1,000 learner choices reject new intent but accept an identical retry', async () => { /* Arrange 1,000 valid decisions in progress.json. */ await assert.rejects(library.decide(newDecision), /history is full/); assert.equal((await library.decide(existingDecision)).decisions.length, 1000); assert.equal(await lockExists(), false); });
